```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.pos = "htbp")
template_dir <- "../../_shared/template"
source(file.path(template_dir, "viscount_rmd_helpers.R"))
library(jsonlite)

mod_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON("extreme_northern_plains.json5", simplifyVector = FALSE)
sett_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON("extreme_northern_plains_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
ledger_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON("extreme_northern_plains_source_ledger.json5", simplifyVector = FALSE)

clean_text <- function (arg0_s) {
  s <- gsub("&", "and", as.character(arg0_s), fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub(" / ", " and ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("_", " ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  trimws(s)
}

fmt_yr <- function (arg0_y) {
  y <- as.numeric(arg0_y)
  if (y < 0) return(paste0(abs(round(y)), "BC"))
  return(paste0(round(y), "AD"))
}

fmt_coord <- function (arg0_coords) {
  lat <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[2]])
  lat_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lat), 2L), if (lat >= 0) " N" else " S")
  lon_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lon), 2L), if (lon >= 0) " E" else " W")
  paste0(lat_s, ", ", lon_s)
}

fmt_pop_series <- function (arg0_pop) {
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(arg0_pop))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(arg0_pop))[ord]
  if (length(yrs) > 6L) {
    keep <- unique(round(seq(1, length(yrs), length.out = 6L)))
    yrs <- yrs[keep]
    vals <- vals[keep]
  }
  parts <- vapply(seq_along(yrs), function (i) {
    paste0(fmt_yr(yrs[i]), ": ", viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i]))
  }, character(1))
  paste(parts, collapse = "; ")
}

sett_list <- unname(sett_json)
peak_vals <- vapply(sett_list, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1))
sett_names <- vapply(sett_list, function (s) as.character(s$name), character(1))
sett_ranked <- sett_list[order(-peak_vals, sett_names)]
top_sett_list <- head(sett_ranked, 45L)

reg_short <- list(
  enp_souris_devils_lake = "Souris-Devils Lake",
  enp_red_river_north = "Red River Valley",
  enp_rainy_lake_of_the_woods = "Rainy River Border"
)

exc_list <- Filter(function (c) identical(c$status, "excluded"), ledger_json$candidates)
exc_top <- head(exc_list, 30L)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles WGS84 coordinates, occupational spans and benchmark population estimates for `r length(sett_list)` excavated Woodland, Northeastern Plains Village and Archaic complexes across Extreme Northern Plains Hydrological Unit 09 (144,29k km²) between 9000BC and 1600AD [@kelly2025; @bird2022p3k14c]. The inventory spans 53 complexes on the Souris Loop and Devils Lake Drift Prairie, including the lower Sheyenne loop (led by Biesterfeldt at 480, Biesterfeldt Earthlodge Town at 450, Shea at 310 and Devils Lake-Narrows at 290, alongside early strandline camps at Moon Lake from 9000BC), 37 sites in the Red River of the North Valley (led by Arvilla at 360, Schocker at 290, Waskish Upper Red Lake at 250 and Orwell at 240, with early beach occupations at Ojata Beach from 8500BC) and 10 Rainy River and Lake of the Woods boreal border stations (led by McKinstry at 360, Grand Mound at 320, Nett Lake at 265 and Big Rice at 245) [@johnson1973arvilla; @stoltman1973laurel; @gregg1994plains; @lenius1990rainy]. Source-ledger reconciliation accounts for 100 included complexes (308 dated observations, averaging 3,08 per site with 59 holding three or more benchmarks) and 102 excluded entries across 202 candidates with zero unaccounted records.

# Background

Archaeological aggregations across HU 09 clustered around post-glacial strandlines, river confluences and seasonal resource bottlenecks rather than dense urban centres [@syms1977cultural]. Along the Rainy River at the outlet of Lake of the Woods and across northern Minnesota wild-rice basins, Laurel and Blackduck communities assembled each spring for lake-sturgeon spawning and erected major earthen burial mounds at McKinstry, Grand Mound, Hannaford, Schocker, Nett Lake and Big Rice [@stoltman1973laurel; @lenius1990rainy].

Further west along the Red River beach ridges, the Sheyenne River bend and the glacial narrows of Devils Lake, Arvilla, Devils Lake-Sourisford and Northeastern Plains Village groups built burial mounds and ditch-fortified earthlodge towns near bison-crossing corridors and woodland-margin farms at Arvilla, Devils Lake-Narrows, Sullys Hill Mounds, Shea, Sprunk and Biesterfeldt [@johnson1973arvilla; @gregg1994plains; @toom2004northeastern].

# Methodology

## Inclusion Criteria and Geospatial Encoding

Candidate complexes were screened against CENTAUR-II criteria requiring WGS84 latitude and longitude coordinates, dated ceramic, earthwork or mound stratigraphy and bounded seasonal-to-multi-season resident group estimates [@bird2022p3k14c; @kelly2025]. Close-pair records falling within 2 km of an existing canonical site under variant names are consolidated as duplicate aliases in the source ledger rather than entered twice, alongside non-habitation extractive stations lacking permanent residential bounds. All temporal benchmarks use GMT+0 calendar years, and Table \ref{tab:summary-extreme-northern-plains} summarises site counts and peak sums across the three divisions.

```{r tbl-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(names(mod_json$regions), function (rk) {
  sub_sets <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region, rk), sett_list)
  peaks <- if (length(sub_sets) > 0) vapply(sub_sets, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1)) else 0
  top_name <- if (length(sub_sets) > 0) sub_sets[[which.max(peaks)]]$name else "-"
  data.frame(
    SubRegion = reg_short[[rk]],
    Included = viscount_fmt_number(length(sub_sets), 0L),
    PeakSum = viscount_fmt_pop(sum(peaks)),
    LeadingSite = paste0(top_name, " (", viscount_fmt_pop(max(peaks)), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Sub-regional distribution of the 100 included sites and peak sums across Extreme Northern Plains HU 09.",
  c("Sub-Region", "Included Sites", "Sum of Site Peaks", "Leading Settlement (Peak)"),
  list(label = "tab:summary-extreme-northern-plains", font_size = "footnotesize")
)
```

## Aggregation-Camp Population Estimation

Site trajectories combine excavated habitation terrace area, hearth counts and contemporaneous seasonal camp sizes inferred from burial-mound demography, fortified village ditch perimeters and ethnographic sturgeon-fishery and wild-rice camp sizes [@stoltman1973laurel; @johnson1973arvilla; @toom2004northeastern]. Peak figures reflect maximum regular seasonal or semi-sedentary occupation rather than fleeting ceremonial gatherings.

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation confirms exact parity between the 100 included complexes (308 dated observations, averaging 3,08 per site with 59 holding three or more benchmarks) and the source ledger, alongside 102 excluded entries (101 duplicate-alias consolidations merged within 2 km of canonical sites, led by Devils Lake-Narrows and Arvilla, plus one unquantified stone quarry at Rustad Quarry), totalling 202 accounted candidates. Site coordinates span 45,52 to 49,27 N and 91,58 to 113,75 W, with CENTAUR-II provenance recorded on every entry. Leading Woodland mound centres crest during the Middle-to-Late Woodland peak (Grand Mound 320 in 400AD; Arvilla 360 in 800AD; Devils Lake-Narrows 290 in 800AD; McKinstry 360 in 1100AD), while fortified Northeastern Plains Village towns on the lower Sheyenne crest later at Shea (310 in 1480AD) and Biesterfeldt (480 in 1600AD) [@kelly2025; @toom2004northeastern]. Figure \ref{fig:settlements-extreme-northern-plains} charts the rank-size hierarchy across all 100 catalogued sites and highlights the leading 15 complexes in Panel B.

# Results

## Leading Settlement Gazetteer

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-extreme-northern-plains} details the top `r length(top_sett_list)` complexes by peak population descending out of the `r length(sett_list)` catalogued sites in HU 09.

```{r tab-gazetteer, results='asis'}
rows <- lapply(top_sett_list, function(e) {
  yrs <- sort(as.integer(names(e$population)))
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population)))
  span_str <- if (min(yrs) == max(yrs)) fmt_yr(min(yrs)) else paste0(fmt_yr(min(yrs)), " to ", fmt_yr(max(yrs)))
  data.frame(
    Settlement = clean_text(e$name),
    State = clean_text(e$country),
    SubRegion = reg_short[[e$region]],
    Coords = fmt_coord(e$coords),
    Span = span_str,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    Series = fmt_pop_series(e$population),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_gaz <- do.call(rbind, rows)
rownames(df_gaz) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_gaz,
  "Top 45 complexes by peak population descending in Extreme Northern Plains HU 09 with coordinates, spans and series.",
  c("Settlement", "State", "Sub-Region", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak", "Benchmark Series"),
  list(label = "tab:gazetteer-extreme-northern-plains", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Excluded Candidates and Source Ledger Audit

Table \ref{tab:ledger-extreme-northern-plains} documents the leading 30 of 102 excluded entries from the source ledger (101 duplicate-alias consolidations and one seasonal stone quarry at Rustad Quarry), capped at 30 rows for display.

```{r tab-ledger, results='asis'}
l_rows <- lapply(exc_top, function(cnd) {
  data.frame(
    Candidate = clean_text(cnd$name),
    State = clean_text(cnd$country),
    Reason = clean_text(cnd$reason),
    Justification = gsub("Existing Verified ", "", clean_text(cnd$justification), fixed = TRUE),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_led <- do.call(rbind, l_rows)
rownames(df_led) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_led,
  "Leading 30 of 102 excluded source-ledger candidates in Extreme Northern Plains HU 09.",
  c("Candidate", "Jurisdiction", "Exclusion Category", "Justification"),
  list(label = "tab:ledger-extreme-northern-plains", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations

Site-level documentation in HU 09 faces three constraints. First, Laurel and Arvilla occupations represent semi-sedentary seasonal aggregations rather than year-round nucleated towns, so site estimates measure peak seasonal co-residence [@stoltman1973laurel; @johnson1973arvilla]. Second, Devils Lake water-level fluctuations submerged or eroded shoreline camps across mid- and late-Holocene highstands [@gregg1994plains]. Third, late pre-contact Blackduck and Selkirk winter hunting camps north of the Rainy River fall outside the USGS HUC-2 polygon and are resolved in the Canadian Prairies and Hudson Bay chapters [@lenius1990rainy; @syms1977cultural].

# Conclusion

Cataloguing 100 complexes across 144,29k km² documents the archaeological hierarchy of the Glacial Lake Agassiz basin from 9000BC beach-ridge camps to sixteenth-century fortified Sheyenne earthlodge villages.
